strategy.summary: CART-12 prices the cart at checkout: 10% bulk discount at 10+ items (summed over line quantities), the SAVE5 coupon ($5 off after the bulk discount, floored at $0, other codes refused), and $4.99 shipping unless discounted goods reach $50 (empty cart costs nothing). All logic is in src/cart.js (cartTotal, bulkDiscount); tests are Vitest unit tests through cartTotal. Reading the code: bulkDiscount uses `itemCount > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items gets no discount, contradicting AC1 and the constant's own doc comment ("at least this many") — that boundary case is expected to fail and will be reported as a defect.
inScope: cartTotal pricing: bulk discount, SAVE5 coupon, unknown coupons, shipping threshold, empty cart
Boundaries: 9/10 items, $49.99/$50 goods, coupon larger than goods
outOfScope: Any UI or API around checkout (none exists in the repo)
Currency rounding beyond the values the cases use
assumptions: cartTotal(items, { coupon }) is the checkout price; items are { price, quantity } as in the existing test
Coupon refusal is a thrown Error; tests check it throws and that the message names the submitted code (the part the test controls)
A cart whose coupon floors the goods at $0 still pays $4.99 shipping, since only an empty cart is shipped free below $50
Coupon codes are matched exactly (case-sensitive), as the code does
openQuestions: Should a coupon bringing goods to $0 on a non-empty cart still be charged $4.99 shipping? The code and a literal reading of AC3 say yes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (sum of line quantities) gets 10% off its subtotal; fewer than 10 gets none.
SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount, the goods never go below $0, and any other coupon code is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when the goods after discounts are $50 or more, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs $0.

defects.title: Bulk discount not applied to a cart of exactly 10 items
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items gets 10% off. src/cart.js bulkDiscount uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD` (threshold 10), so exactly 10 items gets no discount. The constant's own doc comment says "at least this many". Expected `>=`.
defects.evidence: cartTotal([{ price: 10, quantity: 10 }]) returns 100 instead of 90; test marked it.fails passes (i.e. assertion toBe(90) fails).

review.standard: Unit: Arrange / Act / Assert, one action per test
review.summary: The coupon refusal tests call cartTotal twice with the same input, once per matcher, so each test has two Acts and duplicated arrangement.
review.failureScenario: In 'refuses an unknown coupon code with an error' (lines 35-36) and 'refuses a coupon code that differs from SAVE5 only in case' (lines 40-41), the same call runs twice; if the code under test ever became stateful or the inputs drifted apart in one line, the two assertions would check different calls. Hoist the call into one arrow (`const act = () => cartTotal(...)`) and assert `toThrow('SAVE10')` (which already requires a thrown error with that message) once, or keep both matchers on the single arrow.
